I'm explaining this to the Judge now, not repeating the question for you now, Mr. Kulic, so wait. Now, I have been given a Serbian version signed and I am preparing to cross-examine this witness. Then somebody in the Prosecution remembers that a mistake was made here or that this is untenable and then he corrects the English version, but he didn't have time to put the Serbian version right and so I am led astray here. Well, I'm not actually led astray. What is important for me is the English version. What you have received in English has been redacted because somebody had enough brains in the Prosecution to conclude that Mr. Kulic could not occupy a post that didn't exist, and then he says vice premier, whereas here it says that he was vice-president of the SAO which is a post that never existed, neither president nor vice-president of the SAO. That did not exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you will be able to shed some light on this. Did this position exist? What can you say about it? Because you were able to compare the two versions, the B/C/S and the English one. What do you have to say about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Serbian Autonomous Region of Western Slavonia, Your Honour, had an assembly and it had an executive organ that was called a council. Now, in that council, the assembly had a president and the council had a president. I was the vice-president of the council. Now, why that does not -- was not specifically stated, the vice-president of the council of SAO Slavonia, I really don't know, but that's no reason for us not to establish that now. On the 1st of June, 1991 -- well, it's impossible because this is all happening in 1992. On the 1st of June I was in the municipal assembly working there. There was no war at the time. There was no SAO Western Slavonia, and so on and so forth. So if that is sufficient explanation, Your Honour ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you were vice-president. What was the date of that exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the period between the 1st of June to the 30th of April -- the 1st of June, 1992, to the 30th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in 1991 you were neither vice-president nor vice-premier. You were nothing at all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you consider that I can continue under these circumstances, I will comply. However, there are so many defects here that you ought to draw a different conclusion from all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kulic, this statement of yours is replete with phrases with which you express your own uncertainty, doubts, lack of knowledge, and the like, subsequent thinking, and so on. And I'll give you a few examples and a few details. In paragraph 30, for instance, you say: "I don't know how the shipment was conducted," and we're talking about weapons. In that same paragraph you say that: "A tank T-55 which might have had JNA insignia but I'm not sure about that ..." In paragraph 32, you go on to say, "if I remember correctly," - and here is the point, "if I remember correctly," I'd like that underlined - "that the Radical Party of Serbia led by Vojislav Seselj had recruited them via their Belgrade office." And then in paragraph 33 you go on to say, "I believe," you use the word "believe," that's what I want to emphasise "that there were four reasons which compelled many volunteers to join the reservist units." Then in paragraph 34, you say "As far as I remember in November 1991 the volunteer units and the White Eagles came under direct control ..." Et cetera. Then in paragraph 34 again: "I don't remember exactly what the symbols and insignia were, but we called them Chetnik insignia." And then in that same paragraph you say: "I heard that the White Eagles were put up in Vocin." Then in paragraph 35, again: "I heard at the Western Slavonia TO command that the volunteers from Serbia were financed from three sources." Then again in paragraph 37, you say: "I know that Seselj took part in the meeting for which I assume was held in order to discuss the deployment of volunteers from Serbia." Now, from this we see you're doing guesswork, speculating all the time about things you're not certain about, don't know for sure. You feel, you heard, and then you don't know who you heard what you heard from. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, what he -- Mr. Seselj says so decidedly is correct, but his illusions, additional illusions I reject.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Then you say: "I'm not quite sure whether Vuk Draskovic was the leader of the White Eagles," in paragraph 41, for instance. Mr. Kulic, while this combat was going on in Western Slavonia when you were in Vocin, where was your family?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know what my family's got to do with any of this, but I will answer. My family was in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Your wife and your daughter were there, right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no reason to keep secret my personal details, but I don't want to present this to the European public and public all over the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, it's no shame to have a wife and daughter. I assume you're proud of your daughter. What is it that I'm asking you that you think is unpleasant?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The family was in Belgrade. Get to another topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are making it impossible for me to conduct my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In paragraph 41 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not preventing you from putting the question. The witness confirmed that his family was in Belgrade, so --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can he say that his wife and daughter were in Belgrade? Where's the shame there? Where does that touch upon his personal integrity? What is bad in that question of mine? I assume that his wife and daughter are honourable people and that he has no reason to confirm that they were there -- or not to confirm that they were there. As far as I know he has one child. It would make me happy to hear that he had more children, but he has this adult daughter, so why would that be a problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mussemeyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I ask, where is the relevance to this question -- for this question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is relevant about the fact that his daughter, son, or niece are in Belgrade? What is the purpose of it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let me conduct my cross-examination as it should be conducted. You want me to disclose my intentions in advance, which is impermissible when it comes to the Trial Chamber. And now I am going to say that you've destroyed my question completely. In paragraph 41 it says: "In fact, my wife, who worked at the medical centre in Vocin at the time, told me that the volunteers belonged to the White Eagles, or Beli Orlovi, paramilitary organisation,"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because the person who was working in the medical centre, did this person mention the volunteers who belonged to the paramilitary organisation called Beli Orlovi? Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this woman told you that volunteers belonged to that organisation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that she met such people there. That's the information I got.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When did this person tell you that? In what year was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it all refers to 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you add in paragraph 41, and I'm a little bit surprised by this given that you were a captain first class and a reservist in the JNA, you add this: "I am not able to establish a distinction between a paramilitary organisation and another organisation." What did this mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said in my statement that there were several groups that replaced each other. They came and went. Because of the post I held I wasn't able to observe all that and say precisely in such and such a location there was such and such a group which differed in such and such a way from the other group. So I couldn't say that explicitly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think, Mr. Seselj, that your time is up. The registrar will confirm this for me. You've had your time. Mr. Seselj, you have two minutes left. In two minutes one can ask a lot of questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there are many questions I can put. I can put 1.867 questions here, but there's a problem and I'll make use of my two minutes to put just one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In paragraph 42 you say: "I don't know whether Veljko Dzakula had contacts with Seselj, but I believe there was some tension between them." And then in paragraph 44 you go on to say that you heard only after 1992 about a certain individual in connection with Bosnia. And in the same paragraph you say: "I believe that Jovic," this is Mirko Jovic, "was a member of a political party advocating monarchy and its name was something like The Patriotic Movement." And in paragraph 47 you say: "I saw a group of volunteers there, and I'm convinced that they set fire to the house." And in the same paragraph as regards the massacre, "I heard that young local Serbs participated in it whose parents were from Bosnia and volunteers who came from other places." In paragraph 47: "Later on I heard that the volunteers had killed those young men outside Vocin." In paragraph 48: "I assume that the attack was not a planned action. As far as I heard from the villagers, the massacres were carried out by two masked groups of paramilitary soldiers, and that's what I heard from the local people." And in the same paragraph: "I don't have first-hand information." And in paragraph 48 also: "That woman says that on that occasion some Chetniks came to ask whether there were houses in the village where Croats lived, and that's a certain Jovan Kadragojevic [phoen]" who's a relative of your wife Jelena Radosevic. And then you say: "My knowledge is based on what I was told by the local people, Croats and Serbs from Vocin," same paragraph, paragraph 49. According to these local people, two members of the Territorial Defence whose last name was Simic committed some of those murders while they were withdrawing. In my opinion they shot and killed Croat civilians because they were angry that they were being forced to leave and things got out of control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please stop. You're going too fast.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I only two minutes. I don't have time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Then you say in another paragraph when the local people of Lisicine left, that's paragraph 50, the pull-out of Serbian population in Lisicine, and then in paragraph 61 you say: "I have no first-hand information," and then you go on to say "I didn't like --" you're talking about Goran Hadzic. "I didn't really like him," and so on and so forth. Is this, Mr. Kulic, testimony or is it your speculation based on hearsay? Are you testifying to anything here at all?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm testifying to what I experienced, what I underwent, what I have information about, Your Honours. I cannot testify to what you did or said, but I did meet you there, not through my own will.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Kulic, you are here in the capacity of a testus. You are here putting forward your testimony. Your testimony is based on I heard, I believe, someone told me, I heard from someone over there, some people said, I don't have first-hand information. Can a real testus behave in such a way? You're a false testus in this proceedings; isn't that correct, Mr. Kulic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This question is not admissible. I'm turning to the Prosecution. Do you have any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, only one issue I want to touch, and I would like to ask the Registry to show us again 65 ter number 608. It is a document which has already been admitted into evidence under P223 and which is under seal. I want to show this to the witness on the monitor and ask him if he recognises this document. Again, this document is under seal. I think we have to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. You can address the document, put questions about the document, but the document will not be shown outside of this courtroom. Nobody outside of this courtroom will see the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an objection, Mr. President. During the examination-in-chief this witness has already said that he had never seen this document before, and in the summary it says -- in the summary delivered to us by the OTP, it says that he recognised the document during his proofing and now the Prosecutor wants to correct the witness subsequently and that is impermissible. I did not deal with this document in the cross-examination. It was not a subject of cross-examination at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You did not use this document as part of your cross-examination, but during your cross-examination you dealt with the SRS volunteers and this document is related to SRS volunteers. And we have no idea what the Prosecutor wants to do with this document. The best solution is probably to listen to Mr. Mussemeyer. Please ask your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you see this document on your monitor?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You have already shown it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Can you comment on this document again?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It follows from this quite clearly that Mr. Radovan Novacic, who arrived with the first group of volunteers and whom I met, is put at the disposal of the Territorial Defence staff in order to coordinate these. That's what was said. The volunteer units, and this is stated here explicitly, you can see it, they are SRS volunteer units on the territory of the staff of Western Slavonia, and Mr. Novacic is to coordinate the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, yesterday you said that you met the person who signed this document. Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Mr. Zoran Rankic. I was speaking about Mr. Zoran Petkovic [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you're allowing all this. You're not allowing me to put a single serious question in my cross-examination and you're allowing these evident tricks by the OTP. I had the patience to listen to this, to hear the witness' reaction, and it was the witness who corrected, it wasn't Zoran Rankic but Ljubisa Petkovic whom the witness met.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mussemeyer, the witness never said that he had met Zoran Rankic, unless I'm mistaken of course. You told him: "You have met this man."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, with all due respect, I refer to the transcript of yesterday, and it is 4943, lines 20 to 21, and the witness said, if I may read this with your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: "I do claim, Your Honours, that I met Ljubisa Petkovic if it's the same person who signed the documents on sending the first group of volunteers to Ceralije." And again the witness yesterday said on transcript 4470, lines 5 to 9, to the question if he ever met Ljubisa Petkovic, he said: "That's the only individual whom I met officially. I remember the name of that individual because of the document that Mr. Novacic had with him in the team, the first group of volunteers to Western Slavonia, or more specifically to the village of Ceralije, which is where I was." What I want to show is that the witness heard of the name of the person whom he met, and he was referring to this document, saying "The person who signed this document is the person whom I met." And I want to ask the witness if this is possible or not possible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is possible, Your Honours. After a lapse of 17 years I can't really be sure about the connection between first and last names and faces. But I'm sure that I met a certain person in connection with these events, but it would be difficult for people with better memories to remember all this, let alone me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you're still allowing this. Let me remind you that the witness stated yesterday that he never went to the headquarters of the Serbian Radical Party. Then the Prosecutor started correcting him. Then the witness stated that in 1992 he went to the War Staff of the Serbian Radical Party quite by chance and in the statement he made in writing it says that in December 1991 he was in the headquarters of the Serbian Radical Party. You can see what sort of galimatias this is. What is the Prosecutor doing here now? Something that was not rounded off --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm completely lost. Everyone is completely lost. We have a document before us dated 24th of October 1991. We see a stamp. We saw all this indicating that this document is probably a true document. We see the signature of Zoran Rankic. Apparently he's the individual who signed the document on the 24th of October. This document is an authorisation signed by Zoran Rankic. Do you know Zoran Rankic, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, I don't know the gentleman but I may have met him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying to understand the following: Where was this document drafted, in your locality or in Belgrade? Because when you look at the top left corner we see "Territorial Defence Staff, Podravska Slatina."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it says the headquarters of the staff of the Territorial Defence of Podravska Slatina too, so it's -- and it says that the document was compiled in Belgrade on the 24th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apparently the document was drafted in Belgrade. You went to the HQ in February 1992. That's what you told us. In other words, you couldn't have met Mr. Rankic in October because you didn't go there in October. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I didn't say that. By your leave, I was in the office of Western Slavonia, the bureau of Western Slavonia in Belgrade and in that War Staff, so those are two locations in question here. I was in the bureau of Western Slavonia in December 1991, and in the War Staff I went there by chance because I was going with a friend and I was probably in that office. But from my memory I cannot recall now how I can make it sound more convincing here. I can't remember the details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mussemeyer, what are you trying to establish? I don't quite understand what you're trying to establish with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I want to -- the witness was referring to this document, saying: "If Ljubisa Petkovic --" he said: "Your Honours, I met Ljubisa Petkovic if it is the same person who signed the document on sending the first group of volunteers to Ceralije." My aim is to show that the witness erred here, he thought Ljubisa Petkovic who signed this document, it was Zoran Rankic who signed this document, and the witness, instead of meeting Ljubisa Petkovic, he met Zoran Rankic. That is what I want to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Just to add, the description of the person the witness gave yesterday does not fit with Ljubisa Petkovic but it fits with Zoran Rankic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you agree, Witness, that according to this document you did not meet Mr. Petkovic but Mr. Zoran Rankic? Would you agree with that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the description yesterday presented here by Mr. Seselj, quite obviously that's not the person. But I claim once again: I did certainly meet a number of people close to him or close to that because I was interested in it in the bureau of Western Slavonia, the offices. People went there. I went there rarely. So as I said yesterday, there might have been a misunderstanding, but it was not intentional or ill-intended, and I wanted to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. No further questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, could you have met Zoran Rankic, is that possible, or do you rule it out totally.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I certainly met with the responsible person for recruiting and mobilising volunteers from the Radical Party. Now, whether that was Mr. Rankic or Mr. Ljubisa Petkovic, quite obviously Mr. Ljubisa Petkovic wasn't the person but I do not exclude having met him, because quite simply I went to places and came into contact and discussed the topics that only those people knew about. So with all the will in the world from the passage of time, I cannot be precise on that point. But later on I didn't have occasion to meet these people for me to confirm the identity, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the OTP have a photograph of Mr. Zoran Rankic by any chance?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Just a minute, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then the best would probably be to show that photograph to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I must excuse. It's of a very poor quality, but it's the best we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here we go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really cannot confirm whether that is the individual I was with, but I don't exclude the possibility either. If I can see this properly, it's a photograph taken in 2003 apparently, judging by what I see here. And that means as far as the period of time is concerned -- or rather, people change as time goes by so I can't really say one way or the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can't say anything. Very well. Mr. Mussemeyer, do you have any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: No, this is my last question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Witness, on behalf of myself and of my colleagues, I would like to thank you for having come to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can note with satisfaction, although I didn't expect this, that this witness showed at least a little bit of decency and did not agree to confirm this trick on the part of the Prosecutor. So I thank him for that. Despite everything in the cross-examination, he showed that he was an honourable man and did not wish to take part in the Prosecution's plot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj interrupted me whilst I was thanking you for having testified for the Prosecution here in The Hague on a number of events you experienced in your country. Thank you very much. The usher will escort you out of the courtroom. And I would also like to ask her to bring in the following witness who will have protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm being told by the Chamber's legal officer that we need a 15-minute break to set up everything. We'll have a 15-minute break to make the necessary arrangements. We'll resume in 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, we need to go into private session for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, I believe that I can ask the witness some short questions that will essentially give the summary of the anticipated evidence in his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis probably explained how I want things to happen and how things are done in other Chambers. The Prosecution gives a brief summary, saying the witness is coming to testify about such and such events. You have two or three minutes to give this summary. And then, only then, can you ask questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Would the Court like me to do that before discussing the written statement with the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: On either 18 or 19 November 1991, the witness went with his parents to the Vukovar Hospital because he believed there was going to be an evacuation convoy from the hospital. The same morning that he and his family arrived a mixed group of JNA regulars and Territorial Defence members arrived and sealed off the hospital exits and entrances. The morning after this group arrived the witness, along with other men, were ordered out of the hospital and onto buses. There were two to three buses waiting. The buses were guarded by armed JNA soldiers. The buses took the detainees to the JNA military barracks where there were an additional two to three buses. At the barracks there was also a mixed group of soldiers. They insulted and threatened the detainees, one saying "Prepare yourself" or "Get ready, Chetniks." The detainees stayed on the buses for one to two hours and then the buses left the barracks. The detainees were then driven to Ovcara farm. There the witness saw the mixed group of soldiers. The men, the detainees, were directed off the buses. They were then stripped of their belongings, which were thrown into a nearby pile. The detainees were forced to enter a hangar. Inside the witness saw that a mixed group of soldiers had formed a double line, a gauntlet. They carried weapons, such as rifles, iron bars, large pieces of wood. They used these weapons to beat the detainees from the bus. There were approximately 200 to 300 detainees in the hangar at Ovcara. A regular-looking JNA soldier took down the names of these men. Inside of the hangar was a man the witness thought or believes was a JNA officer and he had a whistle and directed the beatings. After the names of the detainees were taken, a group of men came into the building and started beating selected detainees. A person nicknamed "Kemo" was so severely beaten that the witness believes he died from his injuries there in that hangar. The witness saw a group of partially uniformed men kicking him, beating him with weapons, and stamping on his head and body. They made him sing Chetnik songs. Another man, Vladimir Djukic, was brutally beaten with his very own crutches. The JNA officer who had the whistle was present all the time the beatings lasted. Later detainees were taken out in groups of 10 to 20. The men were put on a military truck with a canvas-covered rear. The witness jumped from the rear of this truck and escaped. As he did so he heard gunfire coming from the same direction as the truck. The witness was eventually captured, despite his initial escape. He was detained in Vojvodina and then transferred to Belgrade. He was exchanged in August 1992. And that would conclude the summary, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, also in your binder is 65 ter number 7178, and if you could turn to the blue partition in your binder. Before we discuss this exhibit, Mr. Witness, did you meet with representatives of the OTP on March 2nd and 3rd of 2008?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Did you provide a statement to those representatives about what happened to you and others in 1991 in Vukovar and elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review your written statement in your own language?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: And is your language the Croatian language?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Did the interpreter also interpret for you an English version into Croatian?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Now, if you could look at what is marked in your binder as 65 ter number 7178, looking at the first page, does the first page bear your signature?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: And if you could flip through those other pages, do those other pages at the bottom bear your initials?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: And does that document reflect the date on which you signed -- signed it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: And when was it dated, please?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th of March, 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: And does that statement accurately reflect your recollection of the events described in it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'd move for the admission under seal of this document, 65 ter number 7178.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number P268, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could look at 65 ter number 2830, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, directing your attention to 65 ter number 2830, do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court what that is?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the hospital building and the compound of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Now, there's an "A" and two double lines as well as an "X." Could you describe to the Court what those represent.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "A" marks the place where we went out of the hospital building and the double lines mark the place where we were searched before we were taken to the buses which took us away. "X" marks the place where we went out into the street where these buses were waiting to take us away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: How many buses were there waiting for -- waiting to take you away?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection there were three.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: We'd move for the admission of 65 number -- 65 ter number 2830, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could we have an exhibit number for the photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. P269.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now, Mr. Registrar, if we could go to the collection in 65 ter number 2521A, page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, there is an "A" as well as an arrow. Could you describe for the Court what those represent.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The letter "A" represents the exit to the hospital, the auxiliary exit where we were taken out to be taken to the buses. The arrow shows the direction the buses took towards their destination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Who put those markings on the photos?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I can clarify with the witness, Your Honour. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, because I would have difficulty in accepting premarked photos in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, the previous photograph that we looked at with the "A" and the double lines and the "X", who made those markings?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made those markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: And with respect to 65 ter number 2521A, for the "A" and the directional arrow, who made those markings?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made those markings and drew in those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Now, on this specific photograph there's also the word "centre." Did you put the word "centre" in or did someone else?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not write that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: The word "centre," is that -- what does that represent to you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That represents the direction or rather the position of the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Is that in fact the direction of the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay, when were these markings put? And we still don't know who put the word "centre." I must say I find this a bit irregular.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, during the meeting you had with OTP representatives on March 2nd and 3rd of 2008, did you have an opportunity to review photos and make markings on the photos?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did have an opportunity to make markings on the photos shown me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And I can represent to the Court that "centre" is my writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But please understand the difficulties that the Chamber will have in accepting --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: -- premarked photos. This really isn't going to work. I would suggest you put to him clean photos and ask him to make those markings if this is important for your case.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I -- if I could lay the foundation that the witness in fact did mark these photos on March 2nd and 3rd, would that be sufficient for the Court's purposes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That's okay with me, but I'll need to check with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could now move to page 2 of 65 ter number 2521A.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, did you make the markings that appear on that photograph depicted on page 2 of 65 ter number 2521A?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I made those markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: And what do those markings represent?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those markings represent the direction which the bus moved that drove us in the direction of the fairground in this part of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if we could please move to page 3 of 65 ter number 2521A.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: And looking at this photograph, Mr. Witness, did you make those markings on March 2nd and 3rd of 2008?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did make those markings, the ones you can see on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: And what do they represent?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They represent the continuation of the route, the direction that the vehicles moved, moving to the barracks, the buses I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: And where is this in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the actual centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if we could now move to page 4, the same 65 ter number suite.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: On this page are there markings that you made on March 2nd and 3rd of 2008?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You see the markings of the direction taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Taken by the buses?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The buses took that direction towards the Sajmiste fairgrounds or barracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now moving, Mr. Registrar, to page 5 of that suite.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, did you make the markings that we see on this photograph on March 2nd and 3rd of 2008?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I made those, that information which represent the continuation of the route towards the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: How long did it take you to go from the Vukovar Hospital to the barracks?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ten to 15 minutes, not longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, on this page did you make the markings that appear on this photograph on March 2nd and 3rd of 2008?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I made those markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Could you please describe for the Court what this is a photograph of.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this photograph, on this picture, we can see how the convoy of vehicles, of buses, arrived and the place where they were positioned while we were waiting to continue our journey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Could you describe for the Court the significance of the "X" and the directional arrow that's next to it.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The "X" denotes the spot where there was a large group of people that the people that stayed in that part of town came across. The semi-circular arrow is the position of the buses that we were brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: How many buses were there in this semi-circle that you just described?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While we were arriving there were as many as there had been in front of the hospital, so the three buses mentioned. Now, later on two to three buses joined them from the direction of the fairground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Could you briefly describe for the Court what the people who were denoted by the "X," what -- how were they dressed? And were they armed?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were both armed and dressed differently. They had all sorts of clothes on, military, and non-military. Different clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: What did they do, if anything, while you were there in the buses?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, everybody did something. Some people were standing; others were waiting; others were walking around the bus. Some people were threatening people; some people were singing. Everybody was doing something different, what they thought was best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Prosecutor, you've had 25 minutes, so speed things up, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Registrar, if we could move to page 9 of that same exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could you describe for the Chamber what that represents.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see the hangar I assume at Ovcara, and it shows the entrance or the door where you went in and went out and the position of us detainees and how we had to go through that door, how we entered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: And did you make those markings on page 9 of that exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I made those markings.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And finally, Mr. Registrar, if we could move to 65 ter number 4008A.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, did you review this 65 ter number 4008A and did you make notations of -- next to the people that you recognised during your ordeal?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I made those notations.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could just flip through the following pages, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: These notations that you made, Mr. Witness, in 65 ter number 4008A, they're next to people that you knew; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Have you seen any of those people since you last saw them on -- in November at Ovcara or the hospital or in any of the vehicles that you were in?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you be a bit clearer in your question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: On this exhibit you put the places where you last saw these people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Have you ever seen any of these people since?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I never saw any of them again.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution would move for the admission of the attached 65 ter number 2521A, which is attached to the statement, as well as 65 ter number 4008A, which is also attached to the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Before we do that, Ms. Biersay, I would like you to ask the witness if -- or I can ask the witness myself that question. That probably would be more regular. Mr. Witness, did you in any of these photographs or documents that were shown to you see markings that you had not put yourself? And if you wish to see them again, we can just see them again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no need. It's only that "center," the center of town that remains, but I don't think that's that significant because it's common knowledge where the centre of town is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That may well be so, but you will also understand the Chamber's deep suspicion about any premarked documents that are brought before us as evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, 65 ter number 2521A will be Exhibit number P270, and 65 ter number 4008A will be Exhibit number P271.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, this is my last attempt: Do you wish to cross-examine the witness or do you stand by your previous position? Mr. Seselj, can't you hear? I'm asking you whether you wish to cross-examine this witness or whether you don't wish to cross-examine this witness as you told us yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was listening to the French. It's a nice melodious language. But I don't understand anything, but it was the most pleasant thing for me to listen to it. I've already presented my views and position, Mr. President. I'm not going to repeat it. I'm not going to cross-examine any witness under 92 ter, bis, or quater. I would like to examine someone on 92 quater, but it's a question of legal principle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have a number of brief questions to ask you based on your written statement. From your written statement I understand that you took part in the defence of Vukovar. Can you confirm that for me, please?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took part in the defence of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, you had military status.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you were captured, you were captured as a military man?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you fled from the bus, did no one open fire on you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't jump from the bus. It was a military vehicle. But nobody shot at me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And who recaptured you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was captured by the army in the village of Cerici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How far is that village from Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 15 kilometres, as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you were at the farm we saw on the pictures, mistreatment happened, abuse happened. Who were the ones beating up detainees? Were they military personnel from the JNA? Were they members of the Vukovar TO? Were they civilians dressed in military clothing? According to you, who were the men who mistreated the detainees?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I saw there was not a single civilian. All those who were there were some sort of military or paramilitary groups. It's difficult to say, but at any rate they were in some sort of military organ -- they belonged to some sort of military organised unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How can you tell them apart? How can you say who was a military man and who was a member of a paramilitary organisation?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the greatest difference we could say, since we're dealing with recognising people when you see them, was by their clothing and how they acted and held themselves. But mostly the different clothing they were wearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw that you studied at university. You are an educated man. You were even a reserve officer. And on that basis I'd like to ask you the following question: Those who committed these mistreatment, this abuse - and you said there were both paramilitary and military people - do you have the feeling that there was someone in charge there, there was a command there, or was it just total chaos and were people doing whatever they liked? I'm asking you this question because you were there on the spot. How did you assess the situation, analyse the situation there?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My impression was that it was under some sort of subordination. I think that they knew who was in charge. But there were individual acts which took place without the knowledge of the official structures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was there someone who was in command of all these people? Was there a commander there?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view it was a strongly built man with the whistle who influenced the events there in the hangar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you never found out what his name was, did you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You saw the man with the whistle. Was he dressed in a camouflage uniform? Did he have an insignia, a weapon? Apart from this whistle, what were his distinguishing features?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't have a camouflage uniform. He had a JNA windjammer. He did not have any rank insignia or anything like that so you could recognise what rank he held.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You yourself were trained in the reserve officers school of the JNA. If that man had been a JNA officer, would you have seen it immediately, just looking at him.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certainly, if he had ranks, epaulets denoting rank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But irrespective of his clothing, I'm thinking about his natural authority, his behaviour, the way he gave orders. Did he look like someone from the JNA? Did he look like a JNA officer or someone who just happened to be in command on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's rather a complex approach, but anyway this man did have certain responsibilities. Now, what kind of responsibilities or the level of responsibility I can't say. But certainly he was the most important person, he played the most important role there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. We are not going to go on further about that. We'll have other witnesses to deal with this matter. But there is a question I feel I need to ask you. You were transferred to Vojvodina and then to Belgrade. How come you were transferred so far away? Do you have any explanation for this?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how far I can explain that. They managed our fate so I didn't have -- I didn't wield any influence on that. They decided our fate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought I understood the following. As part of this transfer at some point you went to Sid, there you were questioned by civilian police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Stari Mijankovci [phoen] and then to Sid where the civilian structures, or rather an individual from the civilian structure and from the MUP questioned me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were transferred to Belgrade and you were detained at the Belgrade prison because there was an investigation going on about you. You apparently were charged with rebellion and crimes against humanity. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was first of all taken to Sid, escorted to Sid, and then Sremska Mitrovica, and that's when the proceedings started, if I can use the word, as described. And then I was transferred to Belgrade to the military investigative prison there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'm going to ask the other members of the Bench if they have questions. Yes, my colleague has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you told us that you were captured at Cerici by the JNA, by the army.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The village is called Ceric and it was the reserve force of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the reserve force of the JNA. At paragraph 24 of your statement you talk about soldiers who could be identified as local people and who had uniforms and other clothing. Can you confirm that these were local people and that these were not people coming from other regions of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some people whom I knew were locals of the town of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were there also people from other regions of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question: Amongst the detainees, were there also civilians?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in the hospital, or where?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about those who were captured - we saw the list of all these people - and you recognised a number of them. Were there civilians amongst them also?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were all militarily organised, that they weren't civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are talking about the victims, right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN KULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we are talking about the victims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everyone has asked you questions. This concludes your evidence. Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to provide your assistance to the Court. We are going to draw the blinds now. I'll give the floor to Mr. Mundis for him to talk to us about next week's schedule. The usher will escort the witness out of the courtroom. I suppose you want us to move into private session, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 11th day of March, 2008, at 8.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.47 p.m.,
